reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) discusses general HEA concepts, mechanical properties, and deformation mechanisms but provides no specific support for the key premises about the competition between configurational entropy and specific pairwise enthalpic interactions driving short-range order in nanoalloys. The premises are essentially unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes a single-phase disordered solid solution in HEAs.
Specific favorable atomic pair interactions (e.g., Al–Ni) can drive local chemical clustering (short-range order).
This enthalpically driven clustering can compromise the single-phase disordered state despite entropy stabilization.
Rapid quenching can suppress clustering and preserve a random solid solution.
Extended high-temperature annealing promotes atomic diffusion and local chemical ordering.
